elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement, or upon termination of Teleglobe USA Inc.'s participation in this Agreement, the other Parties shall ...", so both expiry and every termination event (including withdrawal of our participation under 18.1) trigger the obligations.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Operative text says "for a period of not less than ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination"; no six-month assistance period is stated. To reach preferred, change the period to six (6) months.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted subparagraph is silent on pricing; no "at then-current rates" (or any rate) language appears. Preferred requires an express then-current-rates basis for the assistance.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii): "within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Teleglobe USA Inc. all data and information belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Teleglobe USA Inc." — the 30-day clock runs from expiry/termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: No format specification in the inserted text; add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (ii).

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or certification limb exists; add a limb (iii) requiring deletion after return and written certification of such deletion.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Trigger language expressly covers "expiry or termination of this Agreement, or ... termination of Teleglobe USA Inc.'s participation", so the obligations apply after every covered exit event rather than only anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: "(i) at Teleglobe USA Inc.'s request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of not less than ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination" — the floor is 90 days and the request is a customer election, not a timing limitation.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "(ii) within thirty (30) days after such expiry or termination, export and deliver ... all data and information belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Teleglobe USA Inc." — export duty, 30-day deadline anchored to expiry/termination, and all categories of our data covered.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as missing: Paragraph 18 governs withdrawal, decommissioning and liquidation of Segments (18.5-18.7) and 31.4 supplies only a five-year confidentiality tail; nothing imposes exit assistance or data return/export.

All three fallback elements are met by the single inserted subparagraph, so the redline is position-complete at the fallback level; the four unmet preferred elements (six months, then-current rates, machine-readable format, certified deletion) are correctly identified as an upgrade rather than claimed as delivered.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion into the termination Paragraph, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or damages boilerplate, no extra procedures, and no deletion or paraphrase of retained language in 18.1, 18.5-18.7 or 31.4.

Intent preserved: the insertion does not disturb the liquidation, proportional-interest or third-party-liability mechanics, introduces no undefined term, and creates no dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence; the multi-party drafting ("the other Parties shall") matches the consortium structure.
Comment is consistent with the operative text: it states the fallback position and offers the preferred six-month/certified-deletion wording without overclaiming.
